record.title: ScienceIDE paper reports scientific-code environments for agent evaluation and training
record.summary: The arXiv v1 paper describes an infrastructure for packaging scientific codebases with executable checks and generating tasks for agent evaluation, supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. It reports 64 environments from 27 scientific codebases, 2,812 tasks and 1,076 executable checks. On an 85-task hard subset, 15 model–harness systems received one-hour budgets; the highest reported success estimates were 67.1% for Fable 5.1, 64.6% for Opus 5 and 63.1% for Astra. Fable was measured once and the Opus/Astra intervals overlap, so the paper does not establish a stable ordering. The paper also reports selected supervised-learning gains on held-out scientific-code repair and public benchmarks. These are author-reported results; independent reproduction and broader external validation remain open.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors describe ScienceIDE as infrastructure that packages versioned scientific code with executable scientific checks and task factories, allowing verified interactions to support evaluation, supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper reports 64 environments across 27 scientific codebases, 2,812 manufactured tasks and 1,076 executable checks. The task inventory is dominated by repair and implementation; the authors state that the 1,000-environment release remains a development target.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On the 85-task ScienceIDE-Hard subset, the authors compare 15 model–harness systems from eight providers under one-hour task budgets. The highest reported success estimates are Fable 5.1 at 67.1%, Opus 5 at 64.6% and Astra at 63.1%; Fable has a single-attempt estimate and the Opus/Astra repeat intervals overlap, so their ordering is not established.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: For selected supervised fine-tuning comparisons, the authors report higher repair reward on held-out tasks within three scientific codebases and gains on selected public code, reasoning and knowledge benchmarks. Confirmation comparisons use disjoint items and unadjusted intervals; one reported comparison declines.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: A reinforcement-learning experiment reports higher held-out verifier reward after 30 training steps on LAPS and MITgcm-biogeo tasks, but the MITgcm run’s logged validation contains 21 of 23 tasks while a rebuilt 66/21 split is not substituted. Treat this result as provisional.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The preprint does not establish independent reproduction, open-ended scientific discovery, broad performance transfer beyond its task families, or that scientific checks cover all scientifically valid implementations.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent replication of the environment inventory, benchmark results or SFT/RL comparisons was conducted.
The ScienceIDE-Hard leaderboard has uneven repeat coverage; Fable is a single attempt and the Opus/Astra intervals overlap. Fine-grained model ordering is unresolved.
For the MITgcm RL run, the logged validation has 21 of 23 tasks, while the paper notes a rebuilt 66/21 split but does not substitute it for the reported run.
The current tasks are predominantly repair and implementation in computational physics and geoscience; independent external audits and adversarial reward-hacking tests remain open.

brief.importance_rationale: If the approach and learning results generalize, executable scientific environments could expand both evaluation and training beyond static scientific text, affecting agent development across scientific-computing domains. The present evidence is one preprint, with bounded task families, unreproduced results, and known measurement limits.
limitations: Single arXiv v1 preprint; no independent reproduction was conducted.
Evidence concerns reference-verifiable software tasks, predominantly repair and implementation in computational physics and geoscience, not open-ended discovery.
The hard evaluation subset is 85 tasks under one-hour budgets; the paper states that the 1,000-environment release remains a development target.
Factory-generated variants may share code paths and assumptions, so task count alone does not measure independent scientific coverage.
Fable 5.1 has a single-attempt estimate; Opus 5 and Astra repeat intervals overlap, so fine-grained ordering is not established.

The paper says scientific checks cover selected observables and tolerances and do not establish correctness outside those checks; independent external audits and adversarial reward-hacking evaluations remain open.
For one MITgcm reinforcement-learning result, the logged validation has 21 of 23 tasks, while the rebuilt 66/21 split was not substituted.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report 64 environments over 27 codebases, 2,812 tasks, an 85-task cross-model evaluation, selected SFT gains, and two small RL experiments. These are preprint claims with uneven repeat coverage and a noted validation-split issue.
technical.compute_or_cost: The paper reports outcome–cost profiles from archived token rates or harness estimates. These are not current prices; this account does not infer cost-efficiency beyond the paper’s bounded measurements.
technical.demonstrated_result: Direct inspection confirms the arXiv v1 paper describes the infrastructure and reports the stated task inventory and experiments. The empirical performance and transfer results remain author-reported.
technical.implementation_status: The paper presents an open infrastructure and links code/model resources. This activation inspected the paper, not the full environment registry, models or training artifacts.
technical.mechanism: Experts define scientific modules, observables and acceptance policies around pinned repositories. Task factories propose changes; executable validation admits tasks, and verifier-graded interaction trajectories feed evaluation, SFT and RL.
technical.regime: The reported registry has 64 environments across 27 scientific codebases and 2,812 tasks, mostly computational-physics/geoscience repair and implementation. ScienceIDE-Hard covers 85 tasks from 18 environments; 15 model–harness systems receive one-hour budgets. Learning studies use selected Qwen models and held-out tasks.
technical.reproducibility: The paper details check calibration and execution protocols, but the source code, environment registry and full training artifacts were not independently audited or run.
technical.strongest_baseline: Model–harness systems are compared under a common task interface and one-hour budgets; selected SFT comparisons pair initial and tuned checkpoints on the same items. No independent platform or reproduction comparison was inspected.

brief.title: ScienceIDE paper reports scientific-code environments for agent evaluation and training
brief.why_it_matters: If the reported environment and verifier approach generalizes, scientific codebases could supply reusable, outcome-checked training experience rather than only static text or hand-built benchmark tasks. The paper demonstrates a substantial computational-science testbed and selected model-learning results, but its current evidence is mostly repair and implementation in computational physics and geoscience, not open-ended scientific discovery.
